key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface energetics more uniform and faster-stabilizing, indicating a smoother carrier landscape with reduced grain-boundary barriers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can improve solar-cell voltage stability and reduce interfacial losses without changing film morphology.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) distributions before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Track illumination-driven surface photovoltage (SPV) dynamics and wavelength dependence to separate grain-boundary vs grain-interior effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CPD narrowing from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, SPV increasing from ~345 to ~417 mV, and SPV stabilization time constant decreasing from ~840 to ~470 s after passivation.
watch_item: KPFM-derived surface potentials are sensitive to experimental conditions and probe calibration, so the nanoscale interpretation should be validated alongside device-level performance.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
